head_policy.rationale: Mistral-7B (dense, 32L/8KV, native 4096 sliding window). Early 20 layers kept GLOBAL (information-mixing); deep 12 layers use LOCAL window=4096 (information-extraction). Conservative front_full=20 protects RAG recall while still saving deep-layer KV/FLOPs. Same shape as the Qwen3/Llama RedKnot configs in this directory.

head_policy.notes: Llama-3.3-70B optimal: PTR-inspired g15 + local_full + deep retrieval (top_p=0.9).

head_policy.rationale: Qwen3-32B 因 q_norm/k_norm (per-head RMSNorm) 导致 attention 高熵化. 实测前 48 层平均 entropy ≈ 1.0 (近均匀分布, 信息混合层), 任何稀疏化都会污染信息流; 后 16 层 entropy ≈ 0.54 (focused, 信息提取层), 可激进窗口压缩. 策略: 前 48 层 global 全保留, 后 16 层 local M=4096.
head_policy.notes: PTR-inspired layout: shallow=local, deep=global. target_global_ratio=0.15, actual=77/512=0.150 | local→local_full (no RoPE reposition) | deep global→half retrieval (top_p=0.9)

head_policy.rationale: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B is a hybrid MoE model: 60 layers, of which 15 are full_attention (every 4th, full_attention_interval=4 -> idx 3/7/.../59) and 45 are linear_attention (GatedDeltaNet). RedKnot full-attention head-class sparsity is applied ONLY to the full layers. Shallow full layers carry critical early features, so we keep the FIRST HALF+1 full layers DENSE (exact) and sparsify only the DEEP half. Sweet spot from the 397B sweep: keeping the first 9 of 15 full layers dense + head-class (frac_global=0.4, window=2048) on the deep 6 is lossless (dF1=0) and maximizes compute saving. Note frac_global=0.4 pairs with window=2048 (window=4096 dropped F1 at this frac_global; frac_global=0.8 instead needs window=4096).

summary.note: Sweet spot selected on the 397B FP8 triviaqa sweep (lossless dF1=0, total compute save ~46%).

sweet_spot.selection: frac_global=0.4, window=2048, deep_moe_start=24, mass_thresh=0.7. Selected on the 397B reduced sweep (lossless dF1=0, max compute save). Verified on the FP8 model at 32K context (N=5, triviaqa): RedKnot outputs matched the STANDARD baseline (lossless) with 51.8% total compute saving and 2.07x theoretical TTFT speedup. mass_thresh=0.7 consistently saved more MoE compute without accuracy loss; deep_moe_start=24 slightly beat 40.

ffn_or_linear_policy.rationale: Qwen3.5-397B linear-attention (GatedDeltaNet) heads have widely different decay/memory. Short-memory heads use a TOKEN window: window-outside history is reused from the decayed prefix status, window-inside is recomputed (lossless when window >= head memory). GLOBAL heads relay full status; LOCAL heads reset to decayed prefix at window boundaries.

moe.note: Deep MoE layers (>= deep_moe_start_layer=24, i.e. the deep 36 of 60 layers) let tokens with attention-mass < mass_thresh*mean SKIP routed experts (keep shared only). Mass is collected from the deep half of full-attention layers. Sweet spot from the 397B sweep: deep_moe_start=24 + mass_thresh=0.7 maximized MoE compute saving (~46% total) while staying lossless.

summary.note: 397B sweet spot: shallow layers (<24) keep dense-token MoE; deep layers (>=24) use sparse-token MoE skipping ~53% low-mass tokens. window_tok[head] = clamp(ceil(safety * mem_len_token), min_window); >= context => GLOBAL. Layers < dense_prefix_layers stay dense.
